apt.gloss: If someone is apt, they have a natural ability to do something or learn something easily.

apt.en: That comment was particularly apt given the situation.
apt.gloss: If something is apt, it is suitable or appropriate in the circumstances.

apt.en: He is apt to forget his keys if he's in a hurry.
apt.gloss: When someone is likely to do something, they are described as being apt to do it.

insolvent.en: Many companies become insolvent due to mismanagement.
insolvent.gloss: If someone is insolvent, they cannot pay their debts.

resonance.en: The guitar's body gives it a strong resonance.
resonance.gloss: In music, resonance is the rich, clear sound made by instruments or voices.

resonance.en: Her speech had great emotional resonance with the audience.
resonance.gloss: Resonance is the experience of an idea, feeling, or situation feeling deeply meaningful.

resonance.en: The room had great resonance because of the wood floors.
resonance.gloss: Resonance, is the quality of space like a hall, church, or cave that makes speech or music in it sound deep and full.

resonance.en: The resonance frequency of the wine glass is 440 Hz.
resonance.gloss: Resonance is sound that is produced or increased in one object when sound waves hit it.

resonance.en: The resonance of the molecule helps explain its stability.
resonance.gloss: In chemistry, resonance refers to the way some molecules can be represented by more than one structure at the same time.

resonance.en: The singer's voice had a lasting resonance.
resonance.gloss: In music, resonance is the rich, clear sound made by instruments or voices.

resonance.en: The circuit is designed to have resonance at this frequency.
resonance.gloss: In electronics, resonance occurs when a circuit can easily transfer energy at a certain frequency.

emergence.en: The emergence of new technologies has changed the way we live.
emergence.gloss: Emergence is the process of coming into view or becoming important.

emergence.en: The emergence of the butterfly from its cocoon is a delicate process.
emergence.gloss: Emergence is the act of appearing, coming out, or becoming known, often suddenly.

emergence.en: The emergence of life is studied as a complex interaction of chemistry and physics.
emergence.gloss: Emergence is when complex properties or behaviours arise from simple parts interacting together.

flask.en: He took a sip of whiskey from the silver flask in his coat.
flask.gloss: A flask is a small, flat container used for carrying liquids, especially alcohol, in a pocket.

flask.en: The scientist poured the solution into the flask to start the experiment.
flask.gloss: A flask is a container used in laboratories to hold, heat, or mix liquids.

cooperation.en: The project succeeded because of the cooperation between the two teams.
cooperation.gloss: Cooperation is the act of working together to achieve a shared goal.

cooperation.en: International cooperation is needed to solve global problems like climate change.
cooperation.gloss: Cooperation is the act of working together to achieve a shared goal.

regulatory.en: The company must follow all the regulatory requirements set by the government.
regulatory.gloss: A regulatory agency, system, requirement, etc., is one related to rules or laws created by an authority to control how something is done.

regulatory.en: The heart has a regulatory system that ensures a steady rhythm.
regulatory.gloss: A regulatory system, circuit, valve, etc., is one that keeps a process, system, or mechanism, especially a biological one, from moving out of its normal state.

tract.en: They bought a tract of farmland.
tract.gloss: A tract is a large area of land.

tract.en: The digestive tract is responsible for breaking down food.
tract.gloss: A tract is a system of organs or parts in the body that serve a specific function.

tract.en: He printed and handed out religious tracts in the town square.
tract.gloss: A tract is a short piece of writing, often on a religious or political subject.

coherent.en: His argument was clear and coherent.
coherent.gloss: If something is coherent, it is logical and well-organized, making sense as a whole.

coherent.en: Despite the troubles, she remained coherent and explained the situation clearly.
coherent.gloss: If someone is coherent, they are able to speak clearly and logically.

coherent.en: The team was coherent in their approach to solving the problem, which led to their success.
coherent.gloss: If a group is coherent, it works well together, with members who are united or in agreement, often sharing common goals or ideas.

restrictive.en: The new law is very restrictive and limits free speech.
restrictive.gloss: If something is restrictive, it limits or controls what people can do.

permissive.en: The teacher was very permissive with homework deadlines.
permissive.gloss: If someone or something is permissive, they allow a lot of freedom and do not strictly enforce rules or limits.

indicator.en: Meters or gauges are examples of an indicator.
indicator.gloss: An indicator is a pointer that indicates something

indicator.en: Litmus paper is a type of indicator used to indicate the pH of a liquid.
indicator.gloss: An indicator is a substance that is used to indicate the concentration of a substance.

sift.en: Sift the flour to remove the clumps.
sift.gloss: If you sift something, you sieve or strain it.

continual.en: The university was in a process of continual change.
continual.gloss: A continual state or situation happens over a period of time without stop.

continual.en: The continual interruptions made it hard to finish the work.
continual.gloss: Continual actions or events are repeated regularly with little time between, often making them annoying.

bitterly.en: She bitterly complained about the unfair decision.
bitterly.gloss: If someone does something bitterly, they do it with strong negative emotions, such as anger or sadness.

bitterly.en: He cried bitterly after hearing the bad news.
bitterly.gloss: If someone does something bitterly, they do it with strong negative emotions, such as anger or sadness.

bitterly.en: The medicine tasted bitterly of herbs.
bitterly.gloss: If something tastes bitterly of something, it tastes strongly and unpleasantly bitter.

wreath.en: They hung a wreath on the door for Christmas.
wreath.gloss: A wreath is a circular arrangement of flowers, leaves, or branches, often used as a decoration or symbol.

wreath.en: A wreath of poppies was laid at the memorial.
wreath.gloss: A wreath is a circular arrangement placed on graves to honour the dead.

wreath.en: Mist wreathed the mountains at sunrise.
wreath.gloss: If x is wreathed in or with y, it is covered or surrounded by it in a circular or curved way.

wreath.en: The champion was wreathed in glory after winning the final match.
wreath.gloss: If x is wreathed in or with y, it is covered or surrounded by it in a circular or curved way.

wreath.en: They wreathed the statue with flowers.
wreath.gloss: If x is wreathed in or with y, it is decorated with a wreath of y.

taxation.en: Taxation of income is less efficient than a sales tax.
taxation.gloss: Taxation is the system or process of collecting taxes from people or businesses.

taxation.en: High levels of taxation can affect economic growth.
taxation.gloss: Taxation is the amount of money collected through taxes.

professionalism.en: The teacher's professionalism impressed the parents.
professionalism.gloss: Professionalism is the skill, good judgment, and behaviour expected from someone who is trained to do a job well.

professionalism.en: Professionalism among Olympic sports teams has expanded greatly.
professionalism.gloss: Professionalism is the practice of using professionals.

rainforest.en: The Amazon is the largest rainforest in the world.
rainforest.gloss: A rainforest is a thick forest with tall trees that grows in hot, wet places.

frightful.en: The storm caused frightful damage to the town.
frightful.gloss: A frightful event or situation is very bad, unpleasant, or shocking.

frightful.en: They heard a frightful noise coming from the woods.
frightful.gloss: If a frightful dreams, animals, or images cause fear or are very scary.

legendary.en: The legendary King Arthur is said to have ruled Britain.
legendary.gloss: A legendary person, place, or event is famous and remembered in stories, whether real or fictional.

legendary.en: Atlantis is a legendary city believed to have sunk into the ocean.
legendary.gloss: A legendary person, place, or event is famous and remembered in stories, whether real or fictional.

legendary.en: The athlete's performance in the game was truly legendary.
legendary.gloss: If something is legendary, it is very famous or well-known for being impressive or extraordinary.

mechanically.en: The parts of the clock move mechanically.
mechanically.gloss: If something happens mechanically, it happens in a way that uses machines or tools.

mechanically.en: She nodded mechanically during the long meeting.
mechanically.gloss: If someone acts mechanically, they do something automatically, without thinking or feeling.

notably.en: The artist's work was notably praised for its originality.
notably.gloss: If something is notably done, it is worth noticing or is important that it was done.

notably.en: Many countries were represented at the event, notably France and Germany.
notably.gloss: You use notably to introduce a clear or important example.

ego.en: His big ego made it hard for him to admit he was wrong.
ego.gloss: Your ego is your sense of your own importance or self-worth.

ego.en: Freud described the ego as balancing the desires of the id and the rules of the superego.
ego.gloss: The ego is the part of the mind that deals with reality, according to some psychological theories.

alkali.en: soda, potash, and ammonia are examples of alkalis.
alkali.gloss: An alkali is an aqueous solution with a pH value of more than seven.

neuron.en: The brain contains billions of neurons that help control movement and thinking.
neuron.gloss: A neuron is a cell in the body that sends information by electrical and chemical signals.

subsequently.en: He studied law and subsequently became a judge.
subsequently.gloss: If something happens subsequently, it happens after something else in time.

spur.en: The teacher's words spurred him to study harder.
spur.gloss: If you spur someone or something, you encourage or push them to take action.

spur.en: He spurred his horse into a gallop.
spur.gloss: If you spur a horse, you make it go faster by using spurs on your boots.

spur.en: The cowboy wore boots with silver spurs.
spur.gloss: A spur is a sharp metal piece on a rider’s boot used to make a horse go faster.

spur.en: Winning the award was a spur for her to keep writing.
spur.gloss: A spur is something that encourages or motivates action.

diagonal.en: She drew a diagonal line across the page.
diagonal.gloss: A diagonal line goes across from one corner of a rectangular area to the opposite corner.

diagonal.en: The fabric has a diagonal pattern of stripes.
diagonal.gloss: A diagonal marking or direction is roughly 45° relative to a base.

diagonal.en: They walked in a diagonal direction across the field.
diagonal.gloss: A diagonal marking or direction is roughly 45° relative to a base.

diagonal.en: The diagonal of a square divides it into two triangles.
diagonal.gloss: A diagonal is a straight line that connects opposite corners of a rectangular area.

phenomenal.en: She showed phenomenal skill in the competition.
phenomenal.gloss: If something is phenomenal, it is very great or impressive.

phenomenal.en: The scientist studied the phenomenal behaviour of the particles.
phenomenal.gloss: If something is phenomenal, it relates to a phenomenon or something observable.

formidable.en: The boxer faced a formidable opponent in the championship match.
formidable.gloss: If someone or something is formidable, they cause fear, respect, or admiration because they are powerful, strong, or impressive.

formidable.en: Climbing the mountain was a formidable task.
formidable.gloss: If something is formidable, it is very difficult or challenging.

yoga.en: She practices yoga every morning to relax and stay fit.
yoga.gloss: A group of exercises from India that include stretching, breathing, and relaxing.

locust.en: A swarm of locusts ate the farmers' crops.
locust.gloss: A locust is a type of large grasshopper that moves in large groups and destroys crops.

locust.en: The park is full of tall locust trees.
locust.gloss: A locust is a type of tree, such as the black locust or honey locust.

comparatively.en: The cost of living here is comparatively low, though not the lowest.
comparatively.gloss: If something is comparatively small, easy, minor, etc., it is moderately so when measured against other things.

comparatively.en: This model is comparatively lighter than the previous version.
comparatively.gloss: If something is comparatively small, easy, minor, etc., it is moderately so when measured against other things.

economically.en: They planned the trip economically to save on costs.
economically.gloss: If something is done economically, it is done in a way that uses money or resources carefully, without waste.

economically.en: The region grew economically over the past decade.
economically.gloss: If something changes, grows, or impacts economically, it does so in a way that is related to economics or financial matters.

gazette.en: The new law was published in the government gazette.
gazette.gloss: A gazette is an official newspaper that publishes legal announcements, public notices, or important information.

workman.en: The workman repaired the brick wall with great care.
workman.gloss: A man who works, especially one employed in manual or industrial labor.

luminosity.en: The luminosity of the sun is greater than the moon.
luminosity.gloss: Luminosity is how bright something is.

tyrant.gloss: A leader of a country who has total control over everything.

coefficient.gloss: A coefficient is a number or item that acts as a measure of something.
